summary: Over the 14-day analysis period, glucose control is exceptional with a Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) of 99.7%, average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, coefficient of variation of 12.9%, and 0.0% time below range. Basal rates, CR, ISF, and automated loop settings are well-matched to metabolic needs.

analysis_steps.findings: Complete 14-day CGM coverage with consistent 15-minute cadence and zero data gaps exceeding 15 minutes. Active profile and treatment records are complete.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 CGM entries across 14 days; 100.0% coverage percent; 0 gaps > 15 minutes.

analysis_steps.findings: Outstanding glycemic safety with zero time below 70 mg/dL and minimal time above 180 mg/dL (0.3%). Glucose variability is low (CV 12.9%).
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose = 117.0 mg/dL, SD = 15.1 mg/dL, TIR = 99.7%, TAR = 0.3%, TBR = 0.0%. Two brief isolated nightly dips to 70-71 mg/dL self-resolved without active hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal segments effectively hold glucose steady during overnight and fasting windows (102-106 mg/dL mean). Target ranges (90-115 mg/dL) are fully achievable.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight local glucose averages: 00:00 (103.1 mg/dL), 01:00 (104.3 mg/dL), 02:00 (105.7 mg/dL), 03:00 (106.0 mg/dL), 04:00 (107.5 mg/dL).

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate ratios (9-12 g/U) and ISF (40-48 mg/dL/U) are well-calibrated. Postprandial glucose across standard meals returns to baseline within 3 to 4 hours. DIA of 5.5 hours prevents IOB stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: 4-hour postprandial glucose changes average -2 to +8 mg/dL from baseline for breakfast and dinner boluses.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM operate smoothly to handle minor meal excursions without causing late-window hypoglycemia or over-basalization.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_interval_minutes=3, max_smb_basal_minutes=45, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30. Smooth postprandial recovery across all days.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific activation condition toggles (e.g. smb_always_enabled) are null in export.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits (Max Basal 2.4 U/h, Max IOB 8.0 U) provide sufficient headroom for automated loop adjustments while maintaining safe boundaries against insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal (2.4 U/h) is ~2.3x maximum basal segment (1.05 U/h); Max IOB (8.0 U) is proportionate to maximum single meal bolus (~5.8 U).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens and Dynamic ISF enablement flags are null in export, though adjustment factor is set to 100%.

analysis_steps.findings: Weekday breakfast (20 min prebolus, 70% immediate) and dinner bolus timing are highly effective. Weekend brunch (10 min prebolus, 60% immediate) sees a transient 2-hour peak of 188 mg/dL before returning to baseline by 4 hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekday breakfast 120m rise: +33 to +57 mg/dL; Weekend brunch 120m rise: +62 to +70 mg/dL, returning to 115-119 mg/dL at 240m.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared e-carbs strategy for higher-fat Weekend Brunch (20g e-carbs over 120 min) aligns with observed absorption, preventing late-window spikes without inducing hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: 240m glucose post-brunch changes are -11 to +1 mg/dL; 360m changes are -15 to -5 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: All profile, automation, and meal strategy parameters are operating in optimal harmony. No parameter changes are necessary. Verification of unpopulated AAPS profile toggles on-device is recommended for record completeness.
analysis_steps.evidence: Consistent 99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, 12.9% CV across 14 full days of telemetry.

strengths: Time in Range is exceptional at 99.7% with 0.0% time below 70 mg/dL.
Overnight glucose stability is excellent, maintaining flat mean curves between 102 and 106 mg/dL.
Low glycemic variability with a Coefficient of Variation of 12.9% (well below the 36% clinical target).
Meal strategies, prebolus timing, and e-carb settings effectively handle high-carb and mixed meals with clean 4-hour recovery.
issues: Transient postprandial glucose elevation up to 188 mg/dL following Weekend Brunch (10:30 local) before returning to target range at 4 hours.

recommendations.title: Test Slightly Extended Prebolus for Weekend Brunch
recommendations.description: Weekend brunch currently produces a 2-hour peak up to 188 mg/dL (+62 to +70 mg/dL rise) before returning cleanly to baseline by 4 hours. Testing a 15-20 minute prebolus instead of 10 minutes may blunt this spike without increasing total insulin.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Active profile settings achieve 99.7% Time in Range with 0.0% hypoglycemia and optimal overnight stability. No adjustment to basal, CR, ISF, target, or DIA is needed.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Perform a standard overnight fasting glucose check periodically to verify basal adequacy during schedule changes.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all active profile basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA, and target segments unchanged.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current prebolus timing (10-20 min), immediate bolus split (60-70%), active SMB/UAM, and 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes for higher-fat meals.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Meal strategies successfully control postprandial rises and return glucose to target range within 4 hours without causing hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe whether extending the prebolus timing for Weekend Brunch from 10 to 15-20 minutes reduces the transient 2-hour peak of 188 mg/dL.

exceptions.suggestion: Consider testing a 15-20 minute prebolus instead of 10 minutes.
exceptions.rationale: Glucose currently peaks at 188 mg/dL at 2 hours post-meal before returning cleanly to baseline by 4 hours.

implementation_steps: Continue using all current active profile parameters without alteration.
Optional: On your AAPS handset, confirm that SMB activation toggles and Autosens settings match your intended preferences.
Optional: For Weekend Brunch, test extending prebolus timing from 10 to 15-20 minutes while keeping total insulin dosage unchanged.
education: Time in Range of 99.7% and CV of 12.9% indicate exemplary glycemic control.
Prebolus timing helps synchronize insulin peak action with carbohydrate absorption to reduce initial postprandial spikes.
E-carbs (extended carbs in AAPS) allow the automated loop to spread carb absorption over several hours for high-fat/high-protein meals without relying on manual dual/extended pump boluses.
safety_notes: This analysis is for decision-support purposes only and does not constitute medical advice.
Always verify any proposed setting changes independently with your healthcare provider.
Make changes one parameter at a time and monitor glucose closely following any adjustment.
